original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: In CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1662's explicit nonabelian alphabet (paid factors I+([g]+1)xy^T over F2[UT4(F2)], g in {a,b,c}, target I+([z]+1)diag(I_w,0)), can two central targets (w=2) be reached with 14 paid calls when there are no extra roles (r=2)? Exhaustive over counts (4,6,4), which CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1662's written bound forces for 14 calls.
scope_change_reason: Takes the open next question of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1662 (head 01cc02b164ecc4f9d84df3f56a1fe65b88daf390): whether its 14..16 two-target interval is sharp at 14. The card's nonabelian-register premise is kept; the domain is narrowed to r=w=2 so the search is exhaustive.
bottleneck_link: A target-specific tariff for an explicitly larger register alphabet: it prices what two central targets cost in one nonabelian model the three-register obstruction does not cover. Screening result only; no supplier, rank profile or kappa change.
stop_rule: Stop after the exhaustive r=2 (4,6,4) search returns either a formally verified witness or none; do not extend to r>=3 (49 couplings per factor) in this session.
evidence: verify.py: quotient map multiplicative on all 4096 UT4(F2) pairs; GL2(F2) orbit representatives (5582) cover all 33489 zero-sum middle sequences; direct 16-call word passes and its 16 omissions fail; exhaustive search over 20791 profiles per side leaves 208 profile pairs and 3248 words, none of which passes the degree-three quotient or the full formal endpoint. test_package.py adds random formula cross-checks, indexed-versus-brute-force key pairing, planted-word completeness and r=1 driver controls. With https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1680 (head a281330e84e64ad357e35b338796c96144a345ce; written lemma: every 14/15-call two-target word with r>=2 compresses to two roles), this excludes 14 calls for every finite r; that corollary is conditional on CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1680 and not re-derived here.
author: Aaron Wang / navinor
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance from Claude Code in derivation, implementation, verification and writing; no independent human review.

open_questions.question: Is 15 attainable for two central targets at r=2 (and therefore, by CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1680, for every r)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It fixes the exact two-target cost at 15 or shows the direct 16-call word is optimal for every workspace size.
open_questions.first_step: Run this pipeline on the splits (5,6,4), (4,7,4) and (4,6,5) allowed by CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1662's bound.
open_questions.blocked_by: fast_search is specialised to (4,6,4); it needs separate a/c profile sets for unequal counts and seven middle calls (9^7 sequences before symmetry).

open_questions.question: Does CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1680's compression lemma survive an independent check?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The every-r corollary of this package rests on it.
open_questions.first_step: Replay CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1680's compression fixtures through this package's separately written formal checker (formal_ok).
open_questions.blocked_by: The lemma is a written argument; finite fixtures corroborate it but cannot replace proof review.
